messages:
anya: Heads-up – saw a spike in GPU pod evictions in ap-southeast1 around 03:10 UTC. Eviction rate ~3x baseline, mostly tiny-gang jobs getting bounced between AZs.
marc: ugh. any obvious cause? network flaps or node drains?
kai: logs look like taint propagation + scheduler preempt churn. A couple of racks hit conntrack limits earlier, then we had a cascade of soft-evicts.
liz: timeline? which AZ?
anya: ap-southeast1-b mainly. timeline: conntrack issue at 03:08 -> nodal NIC rebind at 03:09 -> scheduler started moving pods at 03:09:30.
sre-tim: sample log snippet: 
```
W 03:09:34 scheduler: pod gpu-train-xyz preempted by higher-priority job; node tainted: nic-unavailable
I 03:09:36 kubelet: eviction threshold triggered: ephemeral-storage, initiating gracefulTerminationSeconds=30
```
marc: gracefulTerminationSeconds=30 is tiny for GPU jobs with warm KV caches. They requeue and become tiny-gang thrash. Can we increase eviction grace window for GPU workloads?
kai: we already have a per-pool override but looks like ap-southeast1 didn't pick it up after the label syncer lagged. Syncer lag was due to high API server latency during the conntrack spike.
liz: options: bump grace to 120s for the GPU taint tolerations, or make scheduler prefer draining less aggressively via preemptBuffer=0.1. Both have cost/latency tradeoffs.
anya: prefer a targeted fix: increase grace window for pods with label workload=gpu and toleration of taint=soft-evict for canary AZ then watch. Less global blast radius.
sre-tim: agree. Also propose: add a short cooldown (60s) on requeueing same pod back to different node to avoid hot-restart loop. Could be scheduler-side or via controller that marks recently-evicted pods with a backoff annotation.
marc: can we do a quick canary? ap-southeast1-b zone only, tag a subset of warmpools with new grace param. ops-bot can patch via rollout.
deploy-bot: deploy request received: patch scheduler-config -> set evictionGraceOverride for selector workload=gpu to 120s in cluster ap-southeast1-b (canary). Will apply in ~2m. :gear:
ops-bot: patch scheduled for canary, setting: 
```
evictionGraceOverride:
  selector: "workload=gpu"
  graceSeconds: 120
  scope: az:ap-southeast1-b
```
ops-bot: also adding requeue-backoff annotation controller = true.
liz: monitoring: look at evictions/sec, pod restart loops, and warmpool warmup latency. I'll add a dashboard panel. If evictions drop and cost increase minimal, we can expand to other AZs.
kai: note: this increases token-hours for reserved capacity if pods stay longer on bad nodes. We should correlate with node-health metrics and still cap at X-minute self-evict if node reports NIC down for >5m.
anya: good call. let's run the canary for 2 hours and then decide. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
